title: Hardcoded production database password in source
detail: Line 10 assigns the literal string `"Aur0ra-Portal-Prod-2026!"` to the module-level constant `DATABASE_PASSWORD`. Committing a real credential to version control permanently exposes it to anyone with repository access, including historical clones. The value is not referenced elsewhere in this file but is available to any importing module.

title: yaml.load() called without SafeLoader — arbitrary object instantiation possible
detail: `load_quota_profile()` opens a caller-supplied file path and passes its contents to `yaml.load(handle.read())` at line 17 without a Loader argument. PyYAML's default Loader allows deserialization of arbitrary Python objects (e.g. `!!python/object/apply:os.system`). If the file at `path` is attacker-controlled, code execution is possible. The caller of this function and the source of `path` are not visible in this file.
owaspCategory: A08 Software and Data Integrity Failures

title: TLS certificate verification disabled in outbound HTTPS request
detail: `fetch_project()` calls `requests.get()` with `verify=False` at line 24, disabling SSL/TLS certificate validation for all connections to `API_BASE`. This makes every request transparent to a network-level attacker who can present a self-signed or fraudulent certificate, enabling credential theft (the Bearer token in the Authorization header) and response tampering.

title: OS command injection via os.system() with unsanitised string interpolation
detail: `export_report()` constructs a shell command string at line 30 by interpolating `project_id` and `destination` with `%s` formatting, then executes it with `os.system()` at line 31. `os.system()` passes its argument to the system shell, so shell metacharacters (`;`, `|`, `$(...)`, backticks) in either parameter allow arbitrary command execution. Neither parameter is sanitised in this file; their origin is unknown without cross-file analysis.
